packets.title: Pattern matching and gitignore at a revision

gate.command: cd mcp-server && npm run build && node test-scope-resolve.mjs

regression: cd mcp-server && npm run build && npx biome check src/
acceptance: Every item of PLAN §3 SC2, its deliverables and its gate list, holds, with the design sections its claims name (§0–§2, as revised in §6).
packets.notes: Gap filled: a path an owner include decides is not unsorted even with no sorting row (§2.2 ranks owner rules over everything); a leading ./ is normalized away, while .., a leading /, .amanuensis, empty and . segments are refused. Gitignore runs check-ignore in a scratch repo with core.excludesFile=/dev/null and core.ignoreCase=false (so the set does not depend on the asking machine's filesystem); the gate also swaps two .gitignore files (same paths, same blobs) to pin the path half of the cache key. scope.ts is not wired into any tool yet (SC3/SC4).

packets.title: Reconciliation core over the survey set

gate.command: cd mcp-server && npm run build && node test-scope-reconcile.mjs

acceptance: Every item of PLAN §3 SC4, its deliverables and its gate list, holds, with the design sections its claims name (§0–§2, as revised in §6).
packets.notes: detect_changes resolves the survey set and reads scope rows, ledger, counts and all four digests inside one IMMEDIATE transaction; scope_digest uses kind 'rule'/'sorting'; standing also requires the recorded scope_mode to equal the current one (a gap-fill), and the unsorted publication refusal runs after the unledgered/absent one so SR1's A17 keeps its own refusal. Fresh stores are sorted mode, so five publishing fixtures now record a product sorting row before reconciling: test-scope-reconciliation (C1 and the A16/A17 world), test-package-artifact, test-finding-partition, test-projection-custody, test-refresh-recovery; staleness marking and subsystem mapping of excluded rows are left to SC11.

packets.title: Consumers of inactive rows

gate.command: cd mcp-server && npm run build && node test-scope-consumers.mjs

regression: cd mcp-server && npm run build && npx biome check src/
acceptance: Every item of PLAN §3 SC11, its deliverables and its gate list, holds, with the design sections its claims name (§0–§2, as revised in §6).
packets.notes: Every consumer reads 'inactive' from ACTIVE_LEDGER_ROW_SQL (the latest reconciliation's scope_exclusions); detect_changes uses its in-transaction excluded set and neither marks nor clears an inactive row's stale flag, so the flag is kept as it was until an include rule reactivates it. Gaps filled: get_attention's empty-state ledger counts and review's unverified-file read also leave inactive rows out; review's changed_files section (the git diff itself) is unchanged; impact decides a changed path new since the last reconciliation at the next detect_changes. The gate sets the excluded arm's row stale by UPDATE to stand for a row flagged before the rule, so each reader is tested on its own.

packets.title: Write guard: evidence attachments and the census

gate.command: cd mcp-server && npm run build && node test-scope-attach-guard.mjs

regression: cd mcp-server && npm run build && npx biome check src/
acceptance: Every item of PLAN §3 SC12, its deliverables and its gate list, holds, with the design sections its claims name (§0–§2, as revised in §6).
packets.notes: requireSurveyScopeForEvidence (helpers.ts) reads each evidence row's file_path and refuses an excluded one before any write; wired into all 14 files of §2.6's second table. Gaps filled without changing a decision: crosswalk.ts (outside the deliverables) is guarded because the census finds resolve_crosswalk_identity's evidence and its provenance accepts repository-evidence ids, through one function covering five tools; review_evaluation_alternatives is exempt (free-text evidence). Decision premises of kind evidence (decisions.ts) and research.ts repository-evidence refs also carry evidence ids under argument names the census does not search; they are unguarded and worth a reviewer's look. The parity entry lists only four tools in refuses, because naming tools that other references instruct would oblige those references to quote the sentence. No existing assertion changed.
